title: GitHub Actions scheduled state-mutating workflows: serialize runs with concurrency group github.workflow, cancel-in-progress false
answers: Why do manual dispatches of the stale or duplicate-PR workflow wait instead of running alongside the nightly cron run?
Scheduled stale-issue, stale-PR, duplicate-PR or flaky-test workflows are running at the same time and mutating labels or comments. How is that prevented?
How do I add a concurrency setting to a new scheduled GitHub workflow that writes to the repo?
Where is the concurrency policy for the cron-driven repo-maintenance workflows defined?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/stale.yml, .github/workflows/stale-prs.yml, .github/workflows/duplicate-prs.yml, .github/workflows/flaky-test-detector.yml. These cron plus workflow_dispatch workflows are the scheduled, state-mutating repo-maintenance jobs (closing stale issues and PRs, flagging duplicate PRs, detecting flaky tests); their top-level concurrency block controls whether a manual dispatch can overlap a scheduled run.
Rule: Use a top-level `concurrency:` block with `group: ${{ github.workflow }}` and `cancel-in-progress: false` for such workflows, so all runs of the same workflow (cron and manual) share one queue and run one at a time without cancelling each other. Do not key the group on `github.run_id`, which gives every run its own group and so no serialization.
Symptom: Per-run groups (`${{ github.run_id }}`) let a manual dispatch start while a cron run was still mutating the same issues or PRs, so the two runs could race on the same state.
Constraints: Applies to workflows whose runs modify shared repo state and should not overlap. Do not turn on cancel-in-progress for these, since cancelling a half-finished state-mutating run could leave it inconsistent. Read-only or independent workflows can keep their own grouping.
applies: GitHub Actions workflow concurrency for scheduled, state-mutating repo-maintenance workflows in .github/workflows.

search: Scheduled state-mutating repository maintenance workflows serialize runs using a top-level `concurrency:` block with `group: ${{ github.workflow }}` and `cancel-in-progress: false`. This applies to cron and `workflow_dispatch` workflows like `stale.yml`, `stale-prs.yml`, `duplicate-prs.yml`, and `flaky-test-detector.yml` that close stale issues and PRs, flag duplicate PRs, or detect flaky tests. Do not key the group on `github.run_id`, which fails to serialize runs, and do not enable `cancel-in-progress` to avoid leaving state inconsistent midway through execution.
